findings.issue: Phase 4 contradicts itself on the architecture of `scripts/lint-i18n-brand-literals.mjs`. The Files section says it is 'standalone (NOT in governance/); landing-specific, mirrors lint-phosphor-marketing-only.mjs'. But `lint-phosphor-marketing-only.mjs` (88 lines, confirmed) has zero calls to `loadGovernanceConfig` — its allowed zones are hardcoded regex arrays. Yet the same Phase 4 says the new script 'reads config via `loadGovernanceConfig("i18nBrandLiterals")`'. These two statements directly contradict each other: a standalone script modeled on phosphor should have hardcoded config, not `loadGovernanceConfig`. The plan cannot be both simultaneously.
findings.location: Phase 4 Files section; scripts/lint-phosphor-marketing-only.mjs (confirmed pattern); scripts/governance/_config.mjs
findings.fix: Pick one model and document it consistently. Option A (mirrors phosphor exactly): the script is fully standalone with hardcoded message-file paths and brand-literal patterns, no `_config.mjs` dependency, no `i18nBrandLiterals` entry in DEFAULTS or `governance.config.json`. This is correct since next-intl message catalogs are not a scaffold-distributed concern. Option B (full governance engine): move the script into `scripts/governance/lint-i18n-brand-literals.mjs`, add a thin wrapper, and add `i18nBrandLiterals` to DEFAULTS + config export (extending the config export from 2 to 3 managed sections). Option A is lower risk and matches the phosphor precedent.

findings.issue: Phase 1 requires that `deriveColorNodes()` lowercases all hex values written to `core.json` (`#0033fe`, not `#0033FE`). But `updateBrandMetadata()` — which runs in the same `brand:apply` pipeline — writes `metadata.ts` with uppercase hex (`#0033FE`, `#0BF1C3`) by calling `JSON.stringify(config.colors)` which preserves the casing from `DEFAULT_BRAND.colors` in `brand-types.ts`. This means the two generated outputs of the same pipeline will have different hex casing for the same color values. The plan's Phase 1 derivability test is described as 'case-insensitive' to paper over this, but the idempotency test (`JSON.stringify(updated, null, 2) + '\n'` must be byte-identical on second run) will fail if `deriveColorNodes()` lowercases then writes, and a subsequent `brand:apply` re-reads the now-lowercase `core.json` value and re-lowercases it — the idempotency test should still pass, but the casing asymmetry between the two generated files is never explained as a deliberate design decision in the plan.
findings.location: Phase 1 TDD task 1 (derivability test) + TDD task 4 (idempotency); scripts/brand-apply.ts:189 (`serialize(config.colors)`); packages/design/brand/src/metadata.ts:66 (#0033FE uppercase confirmed)
findings.fix: Add an explicit design note in Phase 1 stating that `deriveColorNodes()` intentionally lowercases hex when writing DTCG JSON (matching `core.json`'s existing lowercase convention, confirmed), while `updateBrandMetadata()` preserves the casing from `DEFAULT_BRAND.colors` (uppercase, matching `metadata.ts`'s existing convention). This is a correct asymmetry but must be stated — otherwise an implementer reading 'hex.toLowerCase()' will question why `metadata.ts` still has uppercase and may incorrectly 'fix' the serializer.

findings.issue: Phase 4 adds `i18nBrandLiterals` to `DEFAULTS` in `scripts/governance/_config.mjs`, which is described as shipped by `create-sailor` into all scaffolds. But `i18nBrandLiterals` is a landing-specific concern: it governs next-intl message JSON files at `apps/landing/messages/`. A scaffolded project that does not use this exact messages path (or uses a different i18n library) would inherit a dead DEFAULTS entry. Worse, if the standalone `lint-i18n-brand-literals.mjs` is NOT shipped by `create-sailor` (the plan says it is landing specific, consistent with the phosphor model), then the DEFAULTS entry in `_config.mjs` has no consumer in scaffolded projects — it is dead config in the shipped artifact.
findings.location: Phase 4 modification to `scripts/governance/_config.mjs`; `_config.mjs` header comment: 'Reads governance.config.json from the project root... The defaults are relative-pattern regexes against the project root — NO monorepo-absolute paths — so the lints work in a fresh scaffold without any config file.'
findings.fix: Do not add `i18nBrandLiterals` to DEFAULTS in `_config.mjs` if the lint script is standalone and not shipped by `create-sailor`. Standalone, monorepo-specific lints (like phosphor) carry their own hardcoded config and do not register in the shared governance engine. If Option A from finding #2 is chosen (mirrors phosphor), this entry in DEFAULTS is simply removed from Phase 4's scope.

findings.issue: Phase 3 states 'apps/web/package.json — add `@nebutra/brand: workspace:*` (not currently a dep)'. This is confirmed correct. findings.issue: Phase 3 introduces a name collision between the new `getSiteUrl(service: BrandService)` in metadata-helpers.ts and the existing zero-param `getSiteUrl()` in apps/landing/src/lib/seo/site-routes.ts. The plan notes 'DISTINCT from the local zero-param getSiteUrl() (different modules, no collision)', but the refactor tasks (steps 17-26) edit site-routes.ts to use `DEFAULT_SITE_URL = \`https://${brand.domains.landing}\` as const` while leaving the zero-param `getSiteUrl()` in place. The problem is that `DEFAULT_SITE_URL` is typed `as const` narrowing it to the literal string `'https://nebutra.com'`, and it is re-exported from metadata.ts (line 10) and tested directly in __tests__/metadata.test.ts (line 2, 15, 23 — the test asserts `alternates?.canonical === DEFAULT_SITE_URL`). Changing DEFAULT_SITE_URL from a string literal to a template expression `\`https://${brand.domains.landing}\`` breaks the `as const` type (it becomes `string`, not the literal), and the existing test at apps/landing/src/lib/seo/__tests__/metadata.test.ts line 23 will fail because it compares against the import of DEFAULT_SITE_URL which is now a runtime-evaluated string. The plan does not include a task to update this test.

findings.issue: Phase 1 task 3 `runDesignTokensBuild()` adds a WASM-heavy ~15-30s synchronous execFileSync call into brand:apply, which Phase 1 task 1 and 2's arch tests both invoke via `pnpm brand:apply`. The idempotency test (task 4) runs brand:apply TWICE. The existing brand-metadata-drift test (already in CI under `pnpm test:arch`) also calls `pnpm brand:apply`. After Phase 1, every one of those arch test invocations will trigger a full Style Dictionary + resvg-js build. The vitest.arch.config.ts sets a global testTimeout of 30_000ms. A single brand:apply with design-tokens build takes 15-30s, and the idempotency test runs it twice back-to-back. At 30s each, the idempotency test alone will exceed the 30s global timeout. Also document that the existing drift test will now take 15-30s longer and verify the CI `lint-typecheck` job's 30-minute timeout-minutes (line 195) is sufficient.

findings.issue: Phase 3 introduces `@nebutra/brand/metadata-helpers` as a new tsup entry point and subpath export, but Phase 3 task 14 ('Wire subpath export + rebuild') is sequenced AFTER tasks 16-25 which refactor live app files to import `from '@nebutra/brand/metadata-helpers'`. Apps consume the brand package via the workspace `dist/` (the tsup build output), not the raw `src/`. Until `pnpm --filter @nebutra/brand build` runs and produces `dist/metadata-helpers.js` + `.d.ts`, any typecheck or build of apps/web, apps/landing, @nebutra/legal, or @nebutra/marketing will fail with 'Cannot find module @nebutra/brand/metadata-helpers'. Tasks 16-25 run typechecks but task 14 (the build step) comes between tasks 13 and 16 in the numbering — however if a worker implements tasks 16+ before the build step resolves, or if turbo's cached build for brand is stale, all downstream typechecks fail. This is a dependency inversion in the task sequencing.
findings.location: Phase 3 tasks 14-26; packages/design/brand/tsup.config.ts; packages/design/brand/package.json exports field
findings.fix: Reorder Phase 3: task 14 (add subpath export to package.json, add entry to tsup.config.ts, run `pnpm --filter @nebutra/brand build`) must come BEFORE tasks 16-25 (all app refactors). Mark task 14 as a hard gate — do not proceed to any app refactor task until `ls packages/design/brand/dist/metadata-helpers.*` shows both `.js` and `.d.ts`. In the plan text, restructure so the build step is task 14 and all refactor tasks are 15+. Also add `pnpm install` explicitly before the build step since the new `"./metadata-helpers"` export entry must be in package.json before workspace consumers can resolve it.

findings.issue: Phase 8 task 5 states: 'Seed governance.config.json brandLiterals with all 203 paths. Subtract the files already migrated in Phases 3/5 — the count will be lower than 203; verify the actual number after those phases land.' This instruction correctly acknowledges that the 203-file count will be reduced by prior phases. However, Phase 8 is sequenced LAST and depends on ALL prior phases. If the 203 count is re-verified only at Phase 8, but Phases 3 and 5 each commit refactors that remove files from the offender list, there is no ratchet protecting against NEW literals being introduced during the gap between Phase 1 and Phase 8. A developer working on Phase 4 (i18n variabilization) could inadvertently add a new raw 'Nebutra' literal in, for example, a new landing component, and no lint guard will catch it until Phase 8 lands. The plan's option-B guarantee ('new literals fail immediately') does not hold until Phase 8 is complete.
findings.location: Phase 8 task 5; Phase dependency order (ratchet is LAST); the gap between Phases 1-7 and Phase 8
findings.fix: This is inherent to the chosen approach (option B seeds the ratchet last) and the plan already acknowledges it. To reduce blast radius, add a note in the Phase 8 section explicitly stating that the ratchet provides no protection during the implementation window. As a partial mitigation, move the creation of the empty `scripts/governance/lint-brand-literals.mjs` engine and its wiring into `scripts/lint-brand-literals.mjs` to Phase 2 (brand config facts gate), with an explicitly empty allowlist that ONLY covers files touched in Phases 1-2. Then progressively expand the allowlist in each phase as files are migrated. This way any new literal introduced mid-implementation is caught immediately rather than deferred to Phase 8.

findings.issue: Phase 4 task 2 adds `injectBrandVars` to `apps/landing/src/i18n/request.ts` BEFORE editing any message files (task 3). The function substitutes `{brandName}`, `{brandNameCn}` etc. into message values at request time. But the existing `check:i18n` CI step (ci.yml line 273) runs a key-parity and ICU-consistency check via `pnpm --filter @nebutra/landing check:i18n`. If that check validates that ICU placeholders in message JSON are satisfied by actual translation call arguments, adding `{brandName}` as a new placeholder in en.json (task 3) without updating the ICU argument lists at callsites will cause `check:i18n` to fail in CI. The plan does not include any task to audit or update the i18n check configuration to account for the new dynamic brand placeholder injection pattern.
findings.location: Phase 4 tasks 2-3; ci.yml line 273; apps/landing/src/i18n/request.ts
findings.fix: Before committing Phase 4 task 3 (first message file edit), run `pnpm --filter @nebutra/landing check:i18n` locally and confirm it passes with the new `{brandName}` placeholders present in message values. If the i18n checker reports undefined placeholders, either: (a) update the checker's allowlist/config to recognize brand vars as injected-at-runtime (not compile-time ICU args), or (b) verify that `injectBrandVars` resolves the placeholders before the next-intl message pipeline sees them. Add an explicit verification step 'check:i18n passes with placeholders' between tasks 3 and 4.

findings.issue: Phase 3 creates `packages/design/brand/vitest.config.ts` and states 'the workspace glob packages/*/vitest.config.ts does NOT match two-level-deep packages/design/brand'. However Phase 6 also says 'Create vitest.config.ts (if not created in Phase 3 — reuse it)' for a totally different package: packages/platform/repositories. These are two separate packages that each need test infrastructure. But the ordering means Phase 3 is 'dependsOn: Phase 1, Phase 2' while Phase 6 is 'dependsOn: — (independent; can run parallel to 3/4)'. If two engineers implement Phase 3 and Phase 6 in parallel, both will be creating vitest.config.ts files in different packages simultaneously — that is fine. However, Phase 5 also potentially creates a vitest.config.ts for packages/design/brand ('Create packages/design/brand/vitest.config.ts (if not created in Phase 3)'). If Phase 3 is skipped or delayed (e.g. because the Decision 2 and 3 blockers haven't been resolved), Phase 5 will need to bootstrap the same vitest infrastructure for brand from scratch, introducing an implicit ordering dependency between Phase 3 and Phase 5 that the dependency graph does not declare.
findings.location: Phase dependency order (Phase 5 listed as independent of Phase 3); Phase 3 task 1 and Phase 5 'Files Created' section
findings.fix: Mark Phase 5 as dependsOn Phase 3's vitest bootstrap task (task 1 only), or restructure Phase 5 task 2 ('arch test for faviconAssets paths must exist') to explicitly check for and conditionally create vitest.config.ts. Alternatively, create the brand vitest.config.ts in a standalone Phase 0 (pre-requisite infrastructure) so both Phase 3 and Phase 5 can safely assume it exists. This prevents the 'if not created' conditional from being silently skipped.

findings.issue: Phase 1 task 1 adds a new `it()` to the existing `tests/architecture/brand-metadata-drift.test.ts` that dynamically imports `../../scripts/brand-apply.ts` to test `deriveColorNodes`. The test file already uses `execFileSync('pnpm', ['brand:apply'], { stdio: 'pipe' })` which invokes the script via tsx as a subprocess. Mixing a subprocess invocation (for the integration tests) with a dynamic ESM `import()` of a `.ts` file (for the unit test of `deriveColorNodes`) in the same test file creates two different resolution contexts: tsx subprocess vs. vitest's own Node.js module resolver. If vitest cannot resolve `../../scripts/brand-apply.ts` directly (tsx transform not configured for the arch config), the dynamic import will fail with a syntax error or transform error, not a clean 'export not found' error. The plan treats this as the expected RED failure ('import error/undefined') but the actual failure mode may be an uncaught module parse error that aborts the entire describe block.
findings.location: Phase 1 task 1; tests/architecture/brand-metadata-drift.test.ts; vitest.arch.config.ts (no tsx transform configured)
findings.fix: Verify that vitest.arch.config.ts has a `vite.plugins` or `resolve.extensions` entry that handles `.ts` imports from scripts/ via Vite's built-in esbuild transform. If not, add the check: `import { deriveColorNodes } from '../../scripts/brand-apply'` in a separate test file (`tests/architecture/brand-apply-pipeline.test.ts`, which the plan already mentions as optional) rather than inside brand-metadata-drift.test.ts. This isolates the new unit test from the existing subprocess-based tests and avoids polluting the describe block with a module-resolution failure.
